title: WPMS/63/2012 of SMT. PUSHPA DEVI Vs BHIM SINGH AND ORS

paras.text:
IN THE HIGH COURT OF UTTARAKHAND AT NAINITAL
Writ Petition No.63 of 2012 (M/S)
Smt. Pushpa Devi ...........Petitioner
 Versus
Sri Bhim Singh & others .......Respondents
Shri Arvind Vashsiht, learned counsel for the petitioner.
Shri Devesh Ghildiyal, learned counsel for the respondent no.1.
Dated: August 13, 2012
Hon'ble V.K. Bist, J.
Present petition has been filed by the plaintiff/
petitioner for quashing the impugned order dated
17.12.2011 passed by the Additional District Judge/
IIIrd FTC, Dehradun in Civil Appeal No.45 of 2004
"Pushpa Devi Vs. Bhim Singh and others", whereby the
amendment application filed by the petitioner has been
rejected.
2. Brief facts of the case, as narrated in the writ
petition, are that Smt. Premwati w/o Shri Nand
Kishore (defendant no.3) executed a sale deed dated
17.10.1979 in favour of Smt. Parwati Devi w/o Shri
Nain Singh in respect of property bearing khasra
no.658 min. area 0.19 acre 1 bigha and abadi
adjoining to the property area 0.12 acre, out of abadi
khasra plot no.659. Thereafter, on 15.05.1991, another
sale deed was executed by Shri Nand Kishore
(defendant no.3) son of Shri Dhan Singh in favour of
Shri Nand Kishore son of Shri Hari Ram (defendant
no.2) in respect of property bearing khasra no.658 min.
area 0.38 acre and khasra no.659 area 0.07 acre, total

2
area 0.45 acre, situated at Mauza Markham Grant,
pargana Eastern Doon, District Dehradun. It is alleged
that the defendant no.3 has no right to sell the land
bearing khasra no.659 part area 0.07 acre of the above
said Mauza. Thereafter, on 29.05.1991, another sale
deed was executed by Smt. Parwati Devi in favour of
Smt. Pushpa Devi plaintiff/ petitioner in respect of
bhumidhari land bearing khasra no.658 min. area 0.31
acre, out of which 0.12 acre of land is of Abadi,
situated at Mauza Markham Garnt (Kurkawala),
Pargana Parwa Doon, District Dehradun. The
boundaries of khasra no.658, so sold, were wrongly
typed in the sale deed dated 29.05.1991, which were
corrected vide correction deed dated 06.08.1991.
However, the plaintiff/petitioner continued to be in
possession of the whole property shown in the above
deed dated 29.05.1991. Soon after the purchase, the
plaintiff planted various trees. The defendant no.3 filed
a suit against one Shri Ashok Kumar son of Shri
Jeewan Ram and the husband of the plaintiff in respect
of property/agricultural land bearing khasra no.658
min. area 0.56 acre, which included 0.007 constructed
abadi area, situated at Mauza Markham Gant
(Kurkawala), Pargana Parwa Doon, District Dehradun.
The said suit was instituted in the Court of the Munsif,
Dehradun, which was registered as Original Suit
No.236 of 1991. On 26.08.1997, the Civil Court Amin,
after local inspection of the property in suit, submitted
his report. The defendant no.3 also filed SCC Suit No.9
of 1994 for rent and ejectment against the husband of
the plaintiff in the Court of Judge Small Causes

3
(District Judge), Dehradun in respect of the property
situated at khasra plot no.659 in Village Kurkawala,
Mauza Markham Grant, Pargana Parwa Doon, District
Dehradun. The said suit was dismissed on 18.09.1996
and no appeal or revision was filed against the order
dated 18.09.1996. It is alleged that the defendant no.3
does not have any right, title in any of the property
bearing khasra no.658 m. area 0.38 acre or khasra
no.659 m. area 0.07 acre, total area 0.45 acre, situated
in Village Kurkawala, Mauza Markham Grant, Pargana
Eastern Doon, District Dehradun. The defendant no.2
executed a sale deed dated 11.05.2001 in favour of
defendant no.1 in respect of the property in suit. It is
alleged that the sale deed dated 11.05.2001, executed
by the defendant no.2 in favour of defendant no.1, is
void and is without any right & title. The plaintiff is in
possession of the property in suit. As the respondents
were interfering in plaintiff/petitioner's possession, the
plaintiff/petitioner instituted Original Suit No.461/
2001 before the Civil Judge (S.D.), Dehradun, seeking
cancellation of sale deed dated 11.05.2001 and for
permanent injunction. The said suit was dismissed
vide judgment and decree dated 26.08.2004. Against
the order-dated 26.08.2004, the plaintiff/petitioner
filed Civil Appeal No.45/2004 before the Court of
Additional District Judge, F.T.C. IV, Dehradun. Same
is pending consideration. During the pendency of
appeal, the plaintiff/petitioner filed amendment
application in order to elaborate her pleading and in
order to add a claim based upon her long and
uninterrupted possession. On 17.12.2011, the

4
Additional District Judge/IIIrd F.T.C., Dehradun
dismissed the said application. Aggrieved by the order-dated 17.12.2011 passed by Additional District Judge
(FTC -III), Dehradun in Civil Appeal No.45 of 2004
"Pushpa Devi Vs. Bhim Singh and others", present writ
petition has been filed by the petitioner.
3. Learned counsel for the petitioner submitted that
while passing the order impugned, the learned Court
below failed to consider that the amendment sought
was merely explanatory and all the factual foundation
for the aforesaid case was already laid in the Court
below. He further submitted that the Court below failed
to appreciate that the consideration for deciding the
case on merits and the consideration for deciding
amendment application, are totally different and the
law on former aspect cannot be considered for later. He
argued that the order-dated 17.12.2011 passed by
Additional District Judge (FTC -III), Dehradun in Civil
Appeal No.45 of 2004 "Pushpa Devi Vs. Bhim Singh
and others" is a bad order and is liable to be quashed.
4. The respondent no.1 filed counter affidavit, in
which he has submitted that the petitioner has given
wrong description of the property conveyed by Smt.
Premwati w/o Shri Nand Kishore (respondent no.3)
vide registered deed of conveyance dated 17.10.1979 in
favour of Smt. Parwati Devi w/o Shri Nain Singh, as in
the said deed of conveyance dated 17.10.1979, no
mention of khasra No.659 has been made. It is
submitted in the counter affidavit that Smt. Premwati
w/o Shri Nand Kishore (respondent no.3) purchased

5
khasra no.658 area 0.19 acre and khasra no.659 area
0.04 acre from its erstwhile owners-in-possession. It is
submitted that Smt. Premwati was incompetent to
execute any deed of conveyance with regard to land
pertaining to alleged khasra no.659 area 0.12 acre. It is
further submitted that it is wrong to allege that the
respondent no.3 was incompetent to transfer khasra
no.659 area 0.07 acre vide registered deed of
conveyance dated 15.05.1991 in favour of respondent
no.2, rather, the respondent no.3 had duly sold out the
said land to respondent no.2. The respondent no.3
purchased khasra no.659 area 0.12 acre from its
erstwhile owners-in-possession vide registered deed of
conveyance dated 31.03.1971, as such, the respondent
no.3 was duly authorized to execute said deed of
conveyance dated 15.05.1991 with regard to khasra
no.659 area 0.12 acre in favour of respondent no.2, as
per the statutory mandate contained in the provisions
of Section 54 of the Transfer of Property Act, 1882. In
the eyes of law, the petitioner has no locus standi to
interdict said deed of conveyance dated 15.05.1991, as
the petitioner is altogether non-est and foreign to said
khasra no.659. It is submitted in the counter affidavit
that the registered deed of conveyance dated
29.05.1991, executed by Smt. Parwati Devi in favour of
the plaintiff/petitioner, stood corrected vide registered
correction deed dated 06.08.1991. As a result of the
same, the covenants of said deed of conveyance dated
29.05.1991, with regard to possession since 12 years
or the planting of trees, would be understood with
regard to the description of the plot of land, as

6
deciphered in said correction deed dated 06.08.1991. It
is alleged that Smt. Premwati was only authorized to
execute registered deed of conveyance in favour of Smt.
Parwati Devi, and Smt. Parwati was also authorized in
the eyes of law to execute any deed of conveyance only
with regard to khasra no.658, as such Smt. Parwati
Devi being cautious of said facts had executed said
correction deed dated 06.08.1991. It is also submitted
that Original Suit No.236 of 1991 and SCC Suit No.9 of
1994 became redundant in view of the family
settlement arrived at in between the successors-in-interest of Late Dhan Singh. Therefore, after the said
family settlement, there was no need to pursue said
cases by the respondent no.3 and both the suits
dismissed for want of prosecution and in view of the
aforesaid, there was no occasion for the respondent
no.3 to prefer any appeal or revision against the same.
It is further submitted that it is wrong to allege that the
respondent no.3 had no right or title with regard to
property bearing khasra no.658 m area 0.38 acre or
khasra No.659 m area 0.07 acre total area 0.45 acre
situated at village Kurkawala, Mauza Markham Grant,
Pargna Parwadoon, District Dehradun. It is stated that
respondent no.3 had duly purchased khasra no.658
area 0.56 acre from its erstwhile owners-in-possession
vide registered deed of conveyance dated 31.03.1971,
out of which only 0.38 acre was duly conveyed by the
respondent no.3 vide registered deed of conveyance
dated 15.05.1991 in favour of respondent no.2. It is
further stated that the respondent no.3, being owner-in-possession of khasra no.658 area 0.038 acre and

7
khasra no.659 area 0.07 acre total area 0.045 acre,
had duly transferred the same in favour of respondent
no.2 vide registered deed of conveyance dated
15.05.1991 and the respondent no.2 had duly
transferred khasra no.658 area 0.038 acre and khasra
no.659 area 0.07 acre, total area 0.045 acre, vide
registered deed of conveyance dated 11.05.2001 in
favour of respondent no.1.
5. Learned counsel for the respondent no.1
submitted that the learned Appellate Court duly
decided the said amendment application preferred by
the petitioner in conformity and in consonance with the
law of land, as enunciated by the Hon'ble Apex Court.
He also submitted that the petitioner cannot be allowed
to introduce such facts in the pleadings, whereby the
nature of original pleadings or cause of action would be
completely changed. In other words, the petitioner
cannot be permitted to substitute the original cause of
action by another inconsistent cause of action under
the guise of amendment of her pleadings, as the pleas
based on title and adverse possession are mutually
inconsistent and the later does not begin to operate
until the former is renounced. It is further submitted
that as the petitioner never denounced her title over
the suit property nor admitted the title of the
respondent no.1 over the same, she cannot be
permitted to raise the plea of adverse possession by
amendment. It is also argued that even otherwise, the
amendment application moved by the petitioner is an
afterthought and has been moved by her with an

8
oblique motive and malafide intention to displace the
respondents completely from the defence taken by
them before the trial Court. Therefore, the learned
Appellate Court has rightly rejected the said
amendment application filed by the petitioner vide
order dated 17.12.2011.
6. I have heard the learned counsel for the parties
and have perused the papers annexed with the writ
petition.
7. The learned Additional District Judge in the
background of the facts, as stated above, considered
the amendment application of the plaintiff/petitioner
and rejected the same by observing that the suit
instituted by the plaintiff/petitioner was on the ground
of title deed, whereas by way of amendment plaintiff/
petitioner, on the ground of adverse possession,
claimed title. The learned Additional District Judge
held that since the plaintiff/petitioner never claimed
her title, she cannot be permitted to raise plea of
adverse possession by way of amendment. I do not find
any infirmity in the order of the Additional District
Judge. Suit was instituted by the plaintiff/petitioner in
the year 2001. Sole basis of suit was title deed.
Plaintiff/petitioner could have filed amendment
application during the pendency of suit. She did not do
so, even though all facts were in her knowledge. After
loosing the case from the trial Court, she moved
amendment application in the pending appeal. By way
of amendment, the main ground taken in the plaint is
being changed without renouncing earlier claim. In

9
these facts and circumstances, the learned Additional
District Judge rightly rejected her application.
8. Accordingly, the writ petition fails and is
dismissed.
9. No order as to costs.
 (V.K. Bist, J.)
Arpan 13.08.2012
